newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China, HK issues feature.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China, HK issues feature.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered news of China and Hong Kong issues on Wednesday.
China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd's unit signed its US$1.05 billion bridging facility, leaving the underwriters to farm out the loan.
"We haven't yet started syndication," said one of the bankers involved in the deal. "We're still finalising the information package."
He expected to start inviting lower level participation over the next two days.
China Everbright said it expected this syndication to close on June 19.

China Everbright did the loan through a wholly owned subsidiary, Everbright Finance and Investment Co Ltd, and the arrangers are China Construction Bank Hong Kong Branch, China International Capital Corp, China Development Finance Co (HK), HSBC Investment Bank Asia, Goldman Sachs (Asia) Finance and Hang Seng Finance.
The loan is to fund up to 70 percent of the HK$11.4 billion purchase of 7.74 percent of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, which was announced on May 9.

Standard Chartered Bank formally launched its HK$2.0 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue. The three-year certificates were launched at par to float at 20 basis points over the one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return is 25 basis points for top-tier managers.
Standard Chartered is rated A2 by Moody's Investors Service and Single-A by Standard and Poor's Corp.
Application will be made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.

As a U.K. bank, Standard Chartered's debt issues also qualify for a 20 percent risk asset weighting under Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development rules, against 100 percent for non-OECD issuers in Hong Kong.
The pricing is a couple of basis points tighter than the 27 basis points Hongkong Bank paid for its three-year LAF issue launched in April.
Sanwa International Finance launched a U.S.-dollar denominated residential mortgage-backed securities issue to securitise a portion of the mortgage portfolio of Sanwa Finance Hong Kong.
The size of the issue is tentatively set at US$144 million, Sanwa said.
The issuer is Hong Kong Homes Funding Corp (1) Ltd, a special purpose vehicle incorporated in the Cayman Islands.

The notes, which mature in May 2017, were priced and re-offered at par. They will float at 20 basis points over the three-month U.S. dollar London Interbank Offered Rate up to August 2007 and at 45 basis points over three-month dollar LIBOR thereafter.
Fees are 12.5 basis points, split as 7.5 basis points for management and underwriting and five basis points for selling.
The notes are 100 percent guaranteed by MBIA Insurance Corp and are expected to be rated AAA by Standard and Poor's Corp and Aaa by Moody's Investors Service.
Sanwa International Finance is the sole lead manager for the transaction. Sanwa Bank Hong Kong branch is the arranger.

In other debt news, analysts in Thailand said that the country's failing economic health and plunging stock market are expected to precipitate more defaults on debt repayments by local corporate borrowers.
In India, firms and banks said that an official panel's recommendations to make the rupee convertible on the capital account within three years would whet the country's appetite for offshore debt.
